correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the killed-diffusion differential equation and both exit transforms; Erlang survival is exactly a finite derivative of the Laplace exit transform. IID excursions prove P(M<m,N=k)=p_m q_m^k, with proper normalization 0<p,q<1. Exact difference identities and derivatives alpha'=1/omega, kappa'=2/omega prove the dominant m^(ell-1) exponential constants, and the exact conditional CDF yields the two count-conditioned tails, size-biased geometric limit, and Gumbel shift. Standalone code passed 9 independent kernel-flux comparisons, two tail constants per clock order, and 9 Gumbel-CDF checks. All limiting claims rest on the proof, not finite numerics.

value.rationale: The first-passage search radius and completed restart budget are jointly important physical observables; a natural multistage Erlang waiting clock changes their rare-event coupling. The theorem provides exact all-count law, distinct zero-versus-positive reset spatial exponential hazards, and a nonzero clock-order-specific loglog Gumbel centering that the Poisson regime lacks. This supplies a reusable model-specific finite-clock-order spatial-risk prediction rather than a minor numerical parameter shift. No unsupported claims of new general extreme-value theory are made.
